articles.title: AI as tutor or shortcut: The difference may shape student learning
articles.summary: Tech News News: Confessions of complete dependence on AI chatbots, of not being able to think of writing without ChatGPT, are increasingly heard in classrooms and off.
articles.body: Confessions of complete dependence on AI chatbots, of not being able to think of writing without ChatGPT, are increasingly heard in classrooms and offices. While the debate around generative AI gains steam, with Anthropic's chief executive calling this month for the industry to slow the pace of AI capability gains, the effect of AI on Gen Z and Alpha is something everyone is curious about. Will a generation swept by the wave of artificial intelligence still look to develop its own thinking in the formative years of life?A recent study following 26,811 secondary-school students in central China found that after students adopted generative AI, their homework scores rose 18% while the time spent completing homework fell 30%.Then came the closed-book examinations. Within six months, researchers estimated exam scores were 20% lower, and on two high-stakes entrance examinations the estimated declines eventually reached 24% and 18%. The losses were concentrated among students whose unusually high homework scores and unusually fast completion times suggested substantial outsourcing to AI. Students who kept spending as much time on homework as non-users experienced much smaller losses. PISA 2025 shows a similar split at a much larger scale, and it moves the question away from whether students use AI to what they do with it.What PISA actually measuresPISA is the Programme for International Student Assessment, run by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), the Paris-based group of 38 member countries.Held every three years since 2000, the test is taken by 15-year-olds, roughly secondary-school age in India. It is not a syllabus examination. Students are given unfamiliar real-world material and asked to reason with it. Each cycle takes one subject as its main domain, and in 2025 that was science, with reading, mathematics and computational problem-solving alongside.Around the test sit background questionnaires covering home circumstances, attitudes to school, curiosity and, for the first time at this scale, how students use AI chatbots for schoolwork. India has participated once, in PISA 2009+, through schools in Tamil Nadu and Himachal Pradesh. India hasn't taken part since then.However, Indian classrooms are also using AI. A 2025 nationwide survey of more than 5,000 teachers by the Centre for Teacher Accreditation found over 70% already using AI in their teaching, with lesson planning the most common use.AI as a guide and not a substituteMore than 760,000 15-year-olds across 91 countries and economies took part in PISA 2025. Across OECD countries, 45.5% said they used AI chatbots at least weekly to "help me learn". Roughly three in ten used AI that often for specific tasks: 31.2% for preliminary research, 29.7% to summarise assigned reading and 28.8% to draft written assignments.Even after allowing for differences in students' and schools' socio-economic backgrounds, frequent AI use to summarise assigned reading was associated with science scores about 15 points lower, and using it to draft assignments with scores about 14 points lower, according to PISA. The gap for preliminary research was smaller, at about 5 points. When students used AI more broadly to "help me learn", the estimated gap was half a point, too small to be statistically significant. These are OECD's own published estimates, not our calculation.The distinction that matters may therefore be between AI used as learning support and AI used as a task substitute, rather than between AI users and non-users.It may be the case that students already struggling are more likely to ask AI to summarise or draft work, and other differences can remain even after socio-economic background is taken into account. OECD itself cautions against causal interpretation.Technique not technology to blame?A randomised experiment involving nearly 1,000 high-school maths students tested two systems. GPT Base behaved broadly like an ordinary chatbot. GPT Tutor was designed to guide students through problems rather than hand over answers. While AI was available, performance rose sharply and students using GPT Base did 48% better on practice problems than the control group, and those using GPT Tutor 127% better.Sans AI, the result was instructive. Students who had used ordinary GPT Base performed 17% worse on the subsequent unaided exam than students who had never had AI. For the group that had used the guardrailed GPT Tutor, that negative effect essentially disappeared. Unrestricted GPT users often asked for or copied solutions, while users of the guided version were more likely to attempt problems or seek guidance. The same underlying technology produced very different outcomes, depending on whether it supported the student's thinking or replaced it.PISA also weakens the easy explanation that frequent AI users are simply less interested in learning. Daily users of AI "to help me learn" reported greater curiosity than students who never used it for that purpose. About 72% of daily users said they liked learning new things, compared with about 66% of non-users, and daily users also reported seeking help more actively. The pattern is not a straight line, dipping among occasional users before rising among regular ones.Attention in short supplyWe are in the age of instant dopamine hits. Each scroll needs to give some sort of validation, or else a reel gets swiped off in a flash. Teenagers are not immune to this trend, and concerns about what it means for sustained attention are growing. PISA's own reading data shows the strain. The share of students OECD classifies as hasty readers, those who respond quickly and inaccurately, rose from 6.6% in 2018 to 11.4% in 2025. Between 2015 and 2025, average OECD reading performance fell 28 points and mathematics fell 22 points, and the share of students below the basic benchmark in reading, mathematics and science rose from 16% in 2022 to 20% in 2025.PISA has been circling the same anxiety for a decade. Its 2015 report found that students who used computers very frequently performed worse, and that heavy national investment in classroom technology had produced no corresponding gains. By 2022 the concern had moved from access to attention, with about 30% of students reporting that they were distracted while using digital devices in most or every mathematics lesson. The broader decline had already begun before generative AI became widely available. What AI adds is an easier way to avoid practising the skills that are already weakening.Across the OECD, students from more advantaged backgrounds use AI more frequently than disadvantaged students. They are also more likely to be taught how to assess the information AI produces: 67% said they had been given school tasks requiring them to assess AI-generated information, against about 58% of disadvantaged students, a gap of more than nine percentage points.The nuance of AI awarenessSchools might conclude that the answer is simply more AI-literacy lessons. PISA suggests it is not that straightforward. Students who said they had been taught to assess AI-generated information did not consistently score higher in science once socio-economic differences were taken into account. Among students using AI equally often, though, those who also reported school exercises in checking AI-generated information scored about 6 points higher among weekly users and 14 points higher among daily users. Among students who used AI less often, the comparison was negative.These are unadjusted mean scores and not causal evidence. They do, however, raise the possibility that learning how to question AI becomes more relevant once AI is already part of a student's routine.AI making short work of homeworkFor generations, homework meant something. It helped students reflect on what they had been taught and reproduce it. It was essentially a precursor of examination. A person doing homework in a dedicated manner was expected to have got the grasp of the subject. With generative AI, that assumption has bitten the dust. The work bit of homework is often transferred to ChatGPT.For the first few years of generative AI, schools focused on detection. PISA 2025 suggests the harder challenge lies in redesigning assignments so that they still demand real thinking. Teenagers are already using AI. What PISA 2025 leaves open is how much thinking they can hand to a machine before the habit of thinking for themselves begins to weaken. Machine learning without humans learning would be one of the great ironies of the AI age.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: After Satya Niketan collapse, cops take ‘What worries you most?’ to Delhi’s PG hubs
articles.summary: Delhi Police is holding “What worries you?” outreach at Delhi PG and coaching hubs after the Satya Niketan collapse, addressing student safety issues like exposed wires, waterlogging and theft.
articles.body: New Delhi: At 4pm, there was little reason for the police personnel waiting in Karol Bagh to expect a crowd. They had picked a spot surrounded by coaching centres and paying guest accommodations, knowing students would return from classes later in the evening. For now, the road carried its usual traffic, but the students they wanted to speak to were still scattered across the neighbourhood.The wait was part of a new Delhi Police approach to reach out to students living in PGs and rented accommodation, particularly in coaching hubs. The move has gained urgency after the Satya Niketan building collapse, which heightened concerns about their safety.By 5pm, the students began trickling in. One was stopped. Then another. A few stayed back as more joined them. Soon, a small group had gathered around Karol Bagh SHO Karuna Sagar.The first thing the SHO did was share his phone number. Students were told they could contact him directly if they faced a problem or noticed something requiring police attention.Then came the questions. How was the PG? Was there anything around the building that worried them? Did they feel safe walking through the neighbourhood?The answers quickly showed that safety extended far beyond the four walls of their accommodation. It wasn’t just about fire extinguishers, emergency exits or the building’s condition; it was also about what hung overhead, what collected on the road after rain, and what happened on the street outside.Kiran, a UPSC aspirant who has lived in the area for two years, said the recent rains had made him wary of exposed electrical wires and waterlogging. “If these wires fall into the water, there is fear of electrocution. It’s not just about how safe the building is. The overall area should be safe for students,” he said.In 2024, a UPSC aspirant had died of electrocution in west Delhi’s Patel Nagar, highlighting the risks posed by exposed electrical infrastructure during the monsoon.Another student, Abhinav, echoed similar concerns. “The wires are right above our heads. It is pathetic,” he said.Then there were worries beyond electricity. Aejaz, another student, recalled a theft in his lane a few days earlier. Others spoke about rash driving on roads used heavily by students. Some were also worried whether the lane outside was safe, the infrastructure maintained and the journey to their coaching centre free of avoidable risks.With electrical wiring emerging as a major concern, SHO Sagar said the next meeting would involve BSES officials. Issues falling under other agencies are being taken up with the departments concerned, officials said.For the students gathered around the SHO, the exercise offered something significant: they now had a number to call before a concern became a complaint, or a complaint became an emergency.The Karol Bagh interaction was not a one-off exercise. DCP (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said teams from police stations across the city were reaching out to students, PG residents and coaching hubs to understand their concerns. articles.title: Inspired by web series ‘Pritam and Pedro’, Gurgaon man dupes MBA student of 25L
articles.summary: Gurugram man arrested for duping MBA student of Rs 24.6 lakh by posing as counsellor, inspired by cybercrime OTT show; police traced money trail, seized phones.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A 24-year-old man from Gurugram, who took inspiration from a web series on cybercrime, was arrested by the Bangur Nagar police for allegedly duping a management student of Rs 24.6 lakh. Alok K, the accused, had posed as a student counsellor and warned the victim that he would be debarred and his career prospects would be ruined if he did not pay up.Upon arrest, Alok told the police that he was inspired by the antagonist on the OTT show ‘Pritam and Pedro’ and had planned to use social engineering and impersonation to deceive the victim. He also intended to erase his digital footprint.The 21-year-old victim had enrolled in a distance-learning programme for an MBA (finance) with a prestigious management institute in Jan 2026. He paid an annual fee of Rs 1.12 lakh for admission and was assigned a seat by the institute.Soon after, the accused (Alok) got in touch with him over phone and introduced himself as a student counsellor. The two met at a cafe in Juhu after which Alok helped the student complete his admission formalities. The student started to trust him.In June, while the student was appearing for an exam online, an alert popped up on his device screen that copying had been detected. The student immediately called up Alok and informed him that he had not copied. On the last day of the exam, the same alert popped up again and the application crashed. At this, Alok called up the student and inquired whether he had been copying again. At this, the student once again denied any wrongdoing.The student grew nervous when Alok warned him that he would be debarred and blacklisted and would never be able to get an admission in any other university in future. Alok offered to sort out the matter and started demanding money. He also promised to refund fhe money if he was unable to do the job.The student transferred him Rs 24.6 lakh in installments. But Alok refunded him only Rs 1.15 lakh. When the student passed the exam but Alok continued to demand money, the student realized he had been taken for a ride. He then confided in his parents and they lodged a complaint at the Bangur Nagar police station earlier this month.Police surveilled Alok’s phone records and the money trail before tracking his location to Gurugram. He was arrested on Sept 11. Police said Alok used to previously work at a call centre that had been contracted by the management institute to coordinate with all students regarding admissions and counselling. He got the victim’s phone number from the call centre’s database and targeted him. articles.title: Mumbai slumdweller poses as engineer on matrimonial site, rapes doctor
articles.summary: Mumbai’s Waliv police arrested Subhash Satpute for allegedly posing as an engineer on a matrimonial site, raping a Vasai doctor, and using fake accounts.
articles.body: VASAI: Waliv police on Monday arrested a slumdweller from Nalasopara for allegedly raping a 30-year-old doctor from Vasai after posing as an engineer on a matrimonial website and tricking her into meeting him while pretending to be a ‘playboy’.The accused, identified as Subhash Satpute (34), contacted the complainant posing as Kumar Jadhav, an engineer earning Rs 37 lakh annually, on a matrimonial website in June.The doctor liked his profile and agreed to consider the proposal. The accused allegedly told her that she would have to have a physical relationship with a ‘playboy’ to test her sexual compatibility before marriage.Police said Satpute provided her with a phone number and told her to meet the ‘playboy’ at a hotel. She met the man, recorded a video of the sexual act, and sent it to the accused, as instructed.Later, Satpute allegedly refused to marry her, claiming that if he married her, he would die within three months. The woman later learnt that the ‘playboy’ was Satpute.She approached Waliv police, who registered a case under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rape and cheating as well as under the Information Technology Act. articles.title: Protesters face tear gas, lathis after bid to storm police station in Madhya Pradesh
articles.summary: Police used tear gas and lathi-charge to stop a mob from storming Kirnapur police station in Jabalpur after custodial assault allegations; several cops injured.
articles.body: JABALPUR: Police fired around 30 tear-gas shells and resorted to a lathi-charge on Tuesday to disperse a crowd that allegedly tried to storm Kirnapur police station while protesting the alleged custodial assault of a pregnant woman and her husband. The protesters pelted stones at the station, injuring SDOP Deepak Tomar and several other policemen.Police said around 100-200 people gathered outside the station and initially tried to open the gate, demanding that police personnel be brought out. The crowd later entered the premises and allegedly damaged window panes by pelting stones. Police then used force and fired around 30 rounds of tear gas to bring the situation under control.Among those injured in the stone-pelting were SDOP Tomar, inspector Jitendra Chauhan, Shailendra Patel, SDOP’s driver Alok, head constable Varsha, and women constables Ambika and Avisha, besides others.The protest came eight days after allegations surfaced that a pregnant woman and her husband were stripped and assaulted inside Kirnapur police station. The allegations emerged on Sept 8, following which all police personnel concerned were suspended and a special investigation team (SIT) was constituted by senior police officers.The case dates back to Aug 21, when two women visiting the Kirnapur post office allegedly lost Rs 50,000 in cash in two bundles and another Rs 10,000. They lodged a theft complaint the same day. A man and a woman were subsequently identified as suspects and arrested on Sept 1.Police sources said the accused later alleged that they had been assaulted in custody, with one of them showing an injury in the lower thigh region. articles.title: 'I wish I was monster': 48 hours after cryptic Instagram post, woman cop found dead
articles.summary: Ahmedabad woman constable Jhanvi Dabhi found hanging in Gandhinagar rented home 48 hours after cryptic Instagram post; police probe, no suicide note found.
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: A decomposing body of 28-year-old woman constable posted at Shahibaug police headquarters was found hanging at her rented home in Sector 3D of Gandhinagar on Monday night, nearly 48 hours after she posted a cryptic message on Instagram.The deceased, Jhanvi Dabhi, originally from Ahmedabad, had been serving in the police force for five years. She was a divorcee and had been living alone in Gandhinagar.Police suspect Dabhi died around one-and-a-half to two days before her body was discovered. Her landlord alerted police late Monday after noticing a foul smell coming from her room. Sector 7 police reached the house and found her body hanging from a ceiling fan with a dupatta. The body was sent for postmortem and an accidental death report was registered.Two days before her death, Dabhi had uploaded a photograph of herself on Instagram with the message, “I wish I was monster you think I am “. Police are examining her social media activity and mobile phone to determine whether the post was linked to circumstances preceding her death.No suicide note was recovered from her house. Police have seized her phone and are examining her calls, messages and other digital evidence. Investigators are also collecting details about her colleagues and friends from Shahibaug headquarters.Dabhi had a difficult family history. Her mother had remarried after her father’s death. Her brother and sister lived with their paternal aunt in Shamlaji, police said.Dabhi had initially entered into a love marriage. After her husband’s death, she married his elder brother following family and social arrangements. The relationship later developed differences, and the couple divorced around one-and-a-half years ago.Relatives described Dabhi as an independent woman living on her own terms. They said she also enjoyed making Instagram reels. Police are examining whether she faced any personal or financial pressures.Forensic Science Laboratory assistance was being taken to establish the approximate time of death. articles.title: Helicóptero de reportagem cai em Los Angeles e deixa ao menos três mortos | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com a emissora NBC News, ao menos uma das vítimas fatais parecia ser uma pessoa que estava em solo no momento da queda.
articles.summary: De acordo com a emissora NBC News, ao menos uma das vítimas fatais parecia ser uma pessoa que estava em solo no momento da queda.
articles.body:
Helicóptero que caiu próximo ao local de um acidente de ônibus em Los Angeles. — Foto: KABC-TV vía AP

Um helicóptero caiu em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos, e três pessoas foram declaradas mortas no local, informou o Corpo de Bombeiros de Los Angeles nesta terça-feira (15).

Segundo a emissora americana NBC News, a aeronave era um helicóptero de reportagem que cobria um acidente envolvendo um ônibus na região de Chatsworth, bairro localizado no Vale de San Fernando. A NBC informou que o helicóptero pertencia à sua afiliada local, a NBC Los Angeles.

De acordo com a NBC News, o helicóptero caiu em um estacionamento próximo a um centro de armazenamento. Imagens exibidas pela emissora mostraram a aeronave destruída após o impacto.

Durante a programação ao vivo, a apresentadora Colleen Williams afirmou que a emissora havia perdido contato com a equipe a bordo antes de receber a confirmação da queda.

"Sabíamos que era um helicóptero de notícias, sabíamos que tínhamos perdido contato com nossa equipe, e acabamos de receber a confirmação de que o helicóptero caiu pouco antes das 19h", disse a jornalista, segundo a NBC News.

O Corpo de Bombeiros informou que três pessoas morreram no local. Segundo a NBC News, uma quarta pessoa foi levada a um hospital, mas o estado de saúde não foi divulgado.

Ainda de acordo com a emissora, ao menos uma das vítimas fatais parecia ser uma pessoa que estava em solo no momento da queda. A informação foi dada pelo capitão dos bombeiros Branden Silverman.

Helicóptero que caiu em Chatsworth, Los Angeles. — Foto: KABC-TV via AP

Segundo a NBC News, o helicóptero fazia a cobertura de uma colisão entre um ônibus do sistema de transporte público de Los Angeles e um carro de passeio quando caiu.

O Corpo de Bombeiros informou que o acidente entre os veículos ocorreu por volta das 17h e deixou duas pessoas mortas, além de vários feridos.

A NBC News relatou que o helicóptero era uma das várias aeronaves que acompanhavam a ocorrência.

Helicóptero acompanhava um acidente envolvendo um ônibus em Los Angeles. — Foto: KABC-TV via AP

O Corpo de Bombeiros de Los Angeles informou que o Conselho Nacional de Segurança nos Transportes dos Estados Unidos (NTSB, na sigla em inglês) e a Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA) investigarão as causas da queda.

articles.title: Quem era idosa encontrada morta no quintal da própria casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Isabel Brilhador foi encontrada morta no quintal de casa nesta terça-feira (15). Ela estava desaparecida em Campo Mourão desde 4 de setembro.
articles.summary: Isabel Brilhador foi encontrada morta no quintal de casa nesta terça-feira (15). Ela estava desaparecida em Campo Mourão desde 4 de setembro.
articles.body:
Isabel Brilhador, de 65 anos. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A aposentada Isabel Brilhador, de 65 anos, foi encontrada morta no quintal da própria casa em Campo Mourão , no centro-oeste do Paraná, nesta terça-feira (15). A idosa estava desaparecida desde 4 de setembro.

O principal suspeito do crime é Anderson do Nascimento Silva, de 31 anos. Ele está preso temporariamente desde quinta-feira (10). Segundo a polícia, o homem mantinha um relacionamento com a idosa há dois anos . Familiares da vítima não sabiam da relação entre os dois.

A polícia encontrou uma transferência via PIX de aproximadamente R$ 80 mil da conta da idosa para a do suspeito na semana do desaparecimento. A defesa do suspeito nega as acusações e informou que o homem prestará os esclarecimentos para a conclusão dos fatos. Confira a nota completa abaixo.

Ao g1, Valéria Brilhador, filha de Isabel, contou que a mãe era apaixonada por viagens e que compartilhava com a família os locais que iria ou que gostaria de viajar.

Nas redes sociais, há registros da idosa em cidades do Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Santa Catarina, entre outras.

"Ela é uma senhora aposentada. Ela mora sozinha, vive sozinha, então ela gosta de passear [...] Ela sempre postava todo dia alguma coisa no WhatsApp e no Instagram. Gostava de se arrumar, gostava de ir ao salão e cuidar da saúde, cuidava da alimentação, disse Valéria.

Conforme a filha, Isabel mantinha uma vida ativa. Ela participava de circuitos de ciclismo, com distâncias de até 47 quilômetros, ia à academia com frequência e participava de projetos de cantos pela cidade.

A família notou o desaparecimento de Isabel após estranhar o perfil das mensagens enviadas pelo celular da idosa.

"Ela tinha as amigas dela do círculo de amizade dela que falavam com ela todo dia. Então, várias pessoas perceberam o sumiço dela e começaram a se comunicar umas com as outras antes de entrar em contato comigo [...] Ela sempre mandava áudio e, nesta semana [do desaparecimento], desapareceram os áudios das conversas. Era só mensagem escrita", diz Valéria.

Segundo a filha dela, em algumas mensagens, a idosa relatou que ela estaria doente e que ia viajar pelo estado. Valéria tentou ligar para ela, mas não teve retorno.

Familiares foram até o imóvel de Isabel e entraram com a ajuda de um chaveiro. No local, em cima da cama, estavam roupas de uma viagem que a aposentada iria fazer para Curitiba nos próximos dias.

Segundo Luã Mota, delegado do caso, a polícia acredita que a idosa pode ter sido assassinada no final de agosto e que o assassino pode ter enrolado a família por algum tempo pelas mensagens.

"A defesa de Anderson do Nascimento Silva, diante das notícias veiculadas a respeito do desaparecimento de Isabel Brilhador, informa que seu constituinte nega, de forma firme e categórica, qualquer participação nos fatos investigados.

Esclarece-se que o caso ainda se encontra em fase de investigação, sem conclusão definitiva acerca das circunstâncias do desaparecimento de Isabel.

Anderson permanece à disposição das autoridades e prestará todos os esclarecimentos necessários para a elucidação dos fatos.

É importante destacar que a prisão decretada possui natureza temporária, medida cautelar própria da fase investigativa, e não se confunde com prisão preventiva, tampouco representa reconhecimento de culpa ou antecipação de condenação.

A defesa já está adotando as medidas judiciais cabíveis e impugnando a decisão por meio do recurso adequado, por entender que não estão presentes fundamentos concretos suficientes para a manutenção da privação de liberdade.

A defesa de Anderson confia no trabalho das autoridades e acredita que o avanço das investigações demonstrará a ausência de seu envolvimento no desaparecimento."

articles.title: Pessoa mais velha de SC: Maria Hermogênea tem 109 anos e vive em Joinville | G1
articles.standfirst: Nascida em 1917, Maria Hermogênea dos Santos vive em Joinville e foi reconhecida pelo instituto LongeviQuest como a pessoa mais velha do estado.
articles.summary: Maria Hermogênea dos Santos, a pessoa mais velha de Santa Catarina, reside em Joinville e testemunhou fatos históricos globais desde o seu nascimento em 1917.
articles.body:
Aos 109 anos, Maria Hermogênea dos Santos foi reconhecida pelo instituto LongeviQuest como a pessoa mais velha de Santa Catarina . A organização é considerada uma autoridade mundial na pesquisa e validação da longevidade humana.

O reconhecimento ocorreu em julho deste ano, após a morte de Tomásia Machado de Bitencourt, que era considerada a mais velha até então.

Moradora de Joinville , no Norte de Santa Catarina, Maria atravessou mais de um século de história e já viu muita coisa — não literalmente, claro.

Não teve filhos, nem casou. Mas, ao longo da vida, testemunhou acontecimentos que marcaram o mundo, como duas guerras mundiais, grandes transformações tecnológicas do século 20 e a pandemia de Covid-19 , em 2020.

Na lista, estão alguns dos principais acontecimentos históricos que ocorreram paralelamente à vida dela:

🤧Pandemia da Gripe Espanhola (1918–1920)

Maria Hermogênea dos Santos, de 109 anos, é a pessoa mais velha de Santa Catarina — Foto: LongeviQuest/Divulgação

Maria nasceu em 28 de fevereiro de 1917 em Guaramirim , no Norte de Santa Catarina . A infância foi marcada pela perda da mãe, que morreu quando ela tinha apenas três anos.

Maria cresceu ao lado de dois irmãos mais novos. Anos mais tarde, o pai se casou novamente com uma mulher viúva, que já tinha um filho.

O casal teve outros cinco filhos, e Maria passou a fazer parte de uma família com oito irmãos criados juntos.

Maria Hermogênea dos Santos nos aniversários de 107 e 108 anos — Foto: LongeviQuest/Divulgação

articles.title: Botox e emoções: estudos revelam impactos na vida social e sexual | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao congelar músculos da face, a toxina botulínica pode dificultar a leitura de expressões alheias e foi associada a alterações no humor e na função sexual.
articles.summary: O botox e emoções estão ligados, pois a toxina botulínica pode prejudicar a leitura de expressões alheias e impactar a satisfação na vida sexual.
articles.body:
O botox está acabando literalmente com as emoções. E não se trata somente das emoções de personagens interpretados por atores e atrizes com a cara cada vez mais congelada por conta da pressão estética. Mas também das de pessoas físicas que passam pelo procedimento.

Isso porque a toxina botulínica não altera apenas a forma como nosso rosto expressa essas emoções. Ela também afeta a chamada mimética facial, que é a nossa capacidade de imitar e ler o que os outros estão sentindo.

Vai dizer que você nunca ficou com vontade de rir quando viu outra pessoa gargalhando?

Os temidos pés de galinha, por exemplo, se formam quando a gente sorri de forma genuína. É o chamado "sorriso de Duchenne", nome chique para o "sorrir com os olhos".

É por isso que esse tipo de marca é chamado de linha de expressão, porque expressa emoções específicas. Nesse caso, alegria, felicidade, simpatia, por aí vai.

E se você aplica botox para apagar essas linhas, as pessoas podem achar seu sorriso falso e interagir de forma diferente com você.

Além disso, com a cara congelada, você perde a capacidade de imitar as expressões da outra pessoa. Isso atrapalha o cérebro na hora de decodificar as emoções de forma rápida e precisa e pode limitar sua capacidade de entender as pessoas ao seu redor e se conectar com elas.

Estudos recentes descobriram que esse congelamento dos músculos da face pode afetar diretamente como a gente sente essas emoções.

Isso porque essa relação é uma via de mão dupla. Ou seja, a gente não sorri apenas porque está feliz. Muitas vezes, o próprio ato de sorrir deixa a gente feliz.

Tanto é que uma pesquisa mostrou que o congelamento dos músculos responsáveis pelos pés de galinha está associado a um aumento nos níveis de depressão.

Afinal, sem o movimento espontâneo dos olhos, o cérebro deixa de receber o feedback positivo necessário para manter o humor elevado.

Da mesma forma, pessoas que aplicaram botox nas linhas que aparecem entre as sobrancelhas relataram melhora no humor – porque pararam de sentir a tristeza ou a preocupação que faz a testa franzir.

Até aí tudo bem, né? Mas e se eu te disser que o botox pode afetar até mesmo sua vida sexual?

Cientistas observaram que as pessoas involuntariamente contraem os músculos da testa naquela fase de excitação que antecede o clímax. O que, de acordo com a teoria das emoções corporificadas, apoia e intensifica a experiência do prazer.

É por isso que mulheres que congelaram a testa com botox relataram uma queda significativa na função sexual geral, com orgasmos mais difíceis de alcançar – e menos satisfatórios.

Ou seja, a expressão facial é parte ativa do prazer, não apenas um reflexo dele. Mais uma prova de que o corpo e a mente estão bem mais conectados do que muita gente imagina.

articles.title: Gravidez após os 45 anos: avanços da ciência e riscos da gestação | G1
articles.standfirst: Casos recentes de mulheres que engravidaram em idade considerada avançada chamam atenção para os avanços da reprodução assistida. Especialistas explicam quais são as possibilidades e os riscos de uma gestação tardia.
articles.summary: A gravidez após os 45 anos é impulsionada pela reprodução assistida, como a fertilização in vitro e o congelamento de óvulos, mas exige cuidados com a saúde.
articles.body:
Como a ciência tornou possível a gravidez após os 45 anos — Foto: Adobe Stock

Aos 48 anos, a apresentadora Maju Coutinho anunciou que está grávida do primeiro filho. Aos 45, Sabrina Sato está no sexto mês de gestação do seu segundo filho, enquanto a atriz Claudia Raia se tornou mãe aos 55 anos, em 2022. Casos como esses chamam atenção por ocorrerem em uma fase da vida em que a fertilidade feminina já sofreu uma queda acentuada e em décadas atrás era algo extremamente raro de acontecer.

Mais do que exceções, esses casos colocam em evidência o avanço da medicina reprodutiva, que faz com que as mulheres possam contar com técnicas capazes de ampliar as possibilidades de engravidar mesmo quando os ovários já não funcionam tão bem como aos 20 ou 30 anos.

Porém, é preciso cuidado para não se enganar com a impressão de que a idade deixou de ser um obstáculo quando o assunto é gravidez. A medicina evoluiu, mas não conseguiu interromper o envelhecimento do sistema reprodutivo. A quantidade e a qualidade dos óvulos continuam diminuindo com o passar dos anos, e os riscos de uma gestação aumentam com o avançar da idade.

A diferença é que, atualmente, existem formas de contornar parte dessas limitações. Congelamento de óvulos, fertilização in vitro, congelamento de embriões e doação de óvulos são algumas das alternativas disponíveis.

A fertilidade feminina começa a diminuir de maneira mais perceptível a partir dos 30 anos e sofre uma queda acentuada depois dos 35. Isso acontece porque as mulheres já nascem com uma quantidade limitada de óvulos e ao longo da vida essa reserva vai diminuindo a cada mês.

Assim, uma mulher pode continuar ovulando aos 45 anos e ainda assim ter uma chance muito menor de engravidar do que tinha duas décadas antes. Mesmo quando a fecundação acontece, cresce a probabilidade de o embrião apresentar alterações cromossômicas, o que pode dificultar sua implantação, acarretar condições de saúde para o bebê ou aumentar o risco de perda gestacional.

Por isso, uma das principais dificuldades de uma gravidez tardia está no próprio óvulo. "Nascemos com esses óvulos, que ficam sujeitos a doenças, medicamentos, poluição, estresse e tudo que nós passamos ao longo da vida. Isso significa uma alteração na energia celular. Então, ele vai sofrendo um impacto com o tempo e perdendo essa capacidade de produzir energia para a célula. Com isso, o óvulo passa a ter dificuldade de separar os pares de cromossomos para formar um embrião e vêm as alterações", explica Fernanda Polisseni, ginecologista da Associação Brasileira de Reprodução Assistida e professora da Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora (UFJF).

Já nos homens o processo é diferente. Eles produzem novos espermatozoides ao longo da vida, embora existam mudanças relacionadas à idade masculina que também aumentam as chances desses espermatozoides apresentarem condições menos favoráveis para uma fecundação.

O congelamento muda parte dessa situação

O congelamento de óvulos surge como uma opção para as mulheres preservarem seus óvulos enquanto ainda não há essa queda acentuada de qualidade e quantidade devido à idade. A técnica permite retirar óvulos dos ovários, congelá-los e armazená-los para uma utilização futura através da FIV (fertilização in vitro).

A FIV é uma técnica de reprodução assistida em que a fecundação do óvulo pelo espermatozoide ocorre em laboratório, ou seja, fora do corpo da mulher. Após a fecundação, o embrião formado é transferido para o útero na tentativa de iniciar uma gestação.

" Entre os 30 e 35 anos consideramos a idade ideal para fazer esse congelamento , porque é a idade de quem que a mulher ainda tem uma boa quantidade de óvulos com qualidade. É possível congelar depois dessa idade, mas é necessário ter em mente que a chance de conseguir uma gravidez é ajustada de acordo com a idade em que esses óvulos estão sendo congelados", acrescenta Polisseni.

Quando uma mulher congela seus óvulos aos 30 anos e decide tentar engravidar aos 45, por exemplo, são usados os gametas que foram preservados antes da queda mais acentuada da qualidade ovocitária. Assim, mesmo que ela tenha quinze anos a mais, seus óvulos mantêm a idade em que foram coletados e congelados.

Ao manter essa qualidade de quando era mais jovem, aumenta-se as chances de uma fecundação e consequentemente de uma gestação, no entanto, isso não é uma garantia de gravidez, pois nem todos os óvulos descongelados sobrevivem ao processo, são fecundados ou dão origem a embriões capazes de resultar em um nascimento.

Para mulheres nessa situação, que não possuem óvulos adequados para uma tentativa de fertilização, ou que não fizeram o congelamento, existe ainda outra possibilidade que é a doação de óvulos. Nesse caso, os óvulos de uma doadora são fecundados em laboratório e o embrião formado é transferido para o útero da mulher que pretende engravidar.

"Nesses casos, conseguimos reduzir o impacto da idade sobre a qualidade genética do óvulo, mas não eliminamos os efeitos do envelhecimento sobre o organismo da mulher que irá carregar a gestação. Por isso, uma mulher de mais de 45 pode, sim, chegar a uma gestação, mas estamos falando de uma situação muito diferente de uma gravidez natural aos 48 ou 50 anos", diz Larissa Pires, ginecologista e obstetra, especializada em reprodução humana e medicina fetal.

Apesar dos avanços da ciência, depois dos 40 anos, alguns problemas durante a gravidez se tornam mais frequentes. Entre eles estão hipertensão, pré-eclâmpsia, diabetes gestacional, alterações placentárias, parto prematuro e necessidade de cesariana.

"Há também os riscos fetais como aumento de taxa de aborto, aumento de risco cromossômico e aumento do risco de restrição de crescimento fetal por uma placentação inadequada", explica Karina Belickas, obstetra do Hospital e Maternidade Santa Joana.

Isso não significa que toda gravidez depois dos 45 anos será considerada de risco, alto risco ou terá complicações, a idade é apenas um dos fatores avaliados pelos médicos. O estado de saúde da mulher, doenças preexistentes, histórico obstétrico e condições específicas da gestação também influenciam.

Existe uma idade máxima para engravidar?

A resposta, segundo os especialistas ouvidos pela DW, depende de como a gravidez acontece. Naturalmente, a possibilidade de engravidar desaparece com a menopausa, quando os ovários deixam de liberar óvulos regularmente. Mas a medicina reprodutiva consegue, em determinadas circunstâncias, permitir uma gestação depois desse período por meio de óvulos ou embriões previamente preservados ou de óvulos doados.

No Brasil, o Conselho Federal de Medicina estabelece regras para a reprodução assistida e determina 50 anos como idade máxima para mulheres buscarem por técnicas de reprodução assistida. A norma prevê exceções, desde que sejam justificadas pelo médico e que não existam condições que representem risco grave à saúde da paciente.

No caso da atriz Claudia Raia, uma situação curiosa ocorreu, segundo ela. Claudia tentava engravidar através da fertilização in vitro e tomou hormônios para o procedimento. A tentativa inicial não deu certo e não resultou na formação de embriões, mas os hormônios deram um impulso em seu organismo, fazendo com que ela voltasse a ovular naturalmente mesmo estando na menopausa.

Segundo a atriz, a gravidez ocorreu naturalmente após a tentativa de FIV.

A medicina não apagou o relógio biológico

Os avanços da reprodução assistida criaram uma possibilidade que não existia para gerações anteriores e trouxe novas oportunidades para o planejamento da maternidade. Mas especialistas alertam que o congelamento não deve ser interpretado como uma garantia de gravidez no futuro, já que existe uma diferença entre ter óvulos congelados e ter um bebê.

Entre uma coisa e outra estão etapas como descongelamento, fecundação, desenvolvimento embrionário, implantação no útero e evolução da gestação. Cada uma dessas etapas possui possibilidades de falha.

"Também não existe atualmente uma técnica capaz de transformar um óvulo de 45 anos em um óvulo biologicamente equivalente ao de uma mulher de 25 ou 30 anos. É justamente por isso que histórias de gestações tardias precisam ser apresentadas com contexto. Elas mostram que a medicina ampliou as possibilidades de maternidade, mas não eliminou os efeitos do envelhecimento reprodutivo", acrescenta Pires.

Além disso, é necessário ter em mente que apesar de o procedimento de fertilização in vitro ser seguro, ele também tem riscos. "Gravidez obtida por FIV tem muito mais riscos de abortamento, prematuridade, insuficiência placentária e partos mais difíceis" , diz Rosiane Mattar, presidente da Comissão Nacional Especializada em Gestação de Alto Risco da Federação Brasileira das Associações em Ginecologia e Obstetrícia (FEBRASGO).

"Hoje, a mulher tem que estudar, trabalhar, ajudar no sustento da família, quer alcançar sucesso e viver um pouco a vida antes de ter filho, e os métodos contraceptivos melhoraram, garantindo a ela a possibilidade de escolher. Mas é importante que ela saiba que, ao deixar para depois, os riscos vão aumentando, não tem jeito ", acrescenta Mattar.

articles.body:
A sessão dessa terça-feira (15) foi marcada pelo presidente do STF , Edson Fachin, para que o plenário da Corte deliberasse sobre a abertura de uma possível investigação contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, no âmbito do Caso Master. Mas a análise do mérito não chegou perto de ser debatida. Logo na abertura da sessão, os ministros Nunes Marques e Dias Toffoli decidiram não participar do julgamento. Na sequência, o clima de animosidade se instalou e os ministros trocaram ironias, acusações e gritos entre si. Na segunda parte da sessão, o presidente do STF pautou a votação de uma questão de ordem que propunha, entre outras coisas, juntar a análise do caso de Moraes aos questionamentos sobre a condução de Mendonça no Caso Master: Gilmar, Zanin e Moraes votaram a favor; Fachin, Mendonça, Fux e Cármen Lúcia, contra. Dino, que havia se declarado favorável, retirou o voto e pediu vista. Assim, a sessão que escancarou a guerra interna do Supremo terminou sem qualquer decisão.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery conversa com o jornalista Reynaldo Turollo Jr, que acompanhou o dia inteiro de atividades no STF. Turollo e Natuza revisam passo a passo do que aconteceu neste dia histórico para o Judiciário.

articles.body:
Um alpinista ferido foi resgatado de helicóptero após cair durante uma escalada no “Power Dome”, uma parede rochosa na região de Sierra Nevada, no estado da Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos. O resgate aconteceu em 11 de setembro.

Imagens da operação mostram o helicóptero voando próximo à parede rochosa enquanto um socorrista, preso a um cabo, é baixado em direção ao local onde estão o alpinista e outras pessoas. Mais adiante no vídeo, é possível ver o momento em que o alpinista é içado. (Veja acima).

Segundo a Patrulha Rodoviária da Califórnia (CHP), o alpinista precisava ser retirado com urgência e receber atendimento médico. Ele foi socorrido pelo sistema de içamento do helicóptero e levado até uma ambulância que aguardava no local.

De acordo com veículos locais, o homem machucou o pé. Não há informações sobre o estado de saúde dele após o resgate.

Para realizar o resgate, o helicóptero partiu da base no Aeroporto de Paso Robles com uma tripulação de duas pessoas. A operação também contou com um técnico de resgate em helicóptero do Gabinete do Xerife do Condado de Fresno.

A expressão "pobreza de luxo" ganhou espaço nas redes sociais para definir um comportamento marcado pelo consumo de itens e experiências acessíveis por meio de parcelamentos e crédito, enquanto objetivos maiores, como a compra de um imóvel, parecem cada vez mais distantes.

As redes sociais também reforçam essa lógica ao destacar viagens, jantares e bens de consumo, sem mostrar os custos por trás dessas escolhas. É desse encontro entre um futuro visto como distante e a facilidade de consumir no presente que surge a chamada "pobreza de luxo".

articles.title: Dormir bem pode ajudar no desempenho escolar de adolescentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisadores analisaram como fatores como qualidade de sono, tempo de tela, atividade física e alimentação influenciam na saúde mental de adolescentes.
articles.summary: Pesquisadores analisaram como fatores como qualidade de sono, tempo de tela, atividade física e alimentação influenciam na saúde mental de adolescentes.
articles.body:
Dormir bem pode ajudar no desempenho escolar de adolescentes. — Foto: Magnific

Boas noites de sono podem ser essenciais para a saúde mental e o desempenho escolar dos adolescentes . Isso é o que aponta um novo estudo publicado na revista científica "Psychological Medicine".

➡️A partir de dados de participantes entre 10 e 13 anos do estudo Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development, que acompanha crianças e adolescentes nos Estados Unidos, os pesquisadores analisaram como os seguintes quatro fatores influenciam a vida dos adolescentes :

O objetivo era entender de que forma esses hábitos poderiam ajudar a explicar a relação entre sintomas de saúde mental, desempenho acadêmico e problemas sociais entre jovens . Nesse contexto, foram avaliados sintomas de depressão, ansiedade e experiências semelhantes à psicose.

A conclusão foi que a qualidade do sono foi o fator que mais se relacionou com sintomas de saúde mental e desenvolvimento na escola.

👉O sono foi responsável por 18,5% das associações com depressão, 36,3% com ansiedade e 8,3% com perturbações com caráter psicótico.

Segundo Jason Smucny, primeiro autor do estudo e neurocientista computacional do Departamento de Psiquiatria e Ciências Comportamentais da Universidade da Califórnia, o resultado surpreendeu os pesquisadores.

"Esperávamos que o sono fosse importante, mas não imaginávamos que ele se destacaria tão claramente em relação aos outros fatores do estilo de vida, especialmente o tempo de tela", comenta.

Hábitos, saúde mental e desempenho acadêmico

Ainda que a pesquisa mostre que o sono tem papel central na saúde mental e, consequentemente, no desempenho acadêmico, os autores ressaltam que ele não é um único responsável por causar problemas aos adolescentes.

O tempo de tela , por exemplo, apareceu como segundo fator mais importante.

Ele correspondeu a 5% da associação entre ansiedade e funcionamento acadêmico, 6,3% da relação com depressão e 6,2% com experiências semelhantes à psicose .

Atividade física e alimentação parecem ter menos influência, com efeitos menores nas associações analisadas.

O estudo investigou efeitos de mediação , ou seja, analisou quanto esses fatores ajudavam a explicar as associações observadas entre sintomas de saúde mental e desempenho acadêmico.

Isto é, não é possível atribuir um mau desempenho na escola exclusivamente a noites mal dormidas ou excesso no tempo de dela, por exemplo. Mas a pesquisa mostra que esses hábitos podem contribuir para esse cenário.

Outro ponto destacado pelos pesquisadores é que a adolescência é um período crítico do desenvolvimento , no qual frequentemente podem surgir problemas de saúde mental, o que pode estar relacionado a um sono de má qualidade.

As conclusões do estudo reforçam que hábitos saudáveis podem ser essenciais para a melhora da saúde mental de adolescentes.

"Embora não vá resolver todos os desafios de saúde mental, rotinas de sono saudáveis ​são uma maneira prática de apoiar o bem-estar emocional e o funcionamento cotidiano da criança ou do adolescente", analisa Tara Niendam, autora sênior do estudo, professora de Psiquiatria e diretora executiva dos Programas de Psicose Precoce da Universidade da Califórnia.

Mas, mesmo que rotinas mais estabelecidas de sono e a restrição de tempo de tela sejam importantes para melhorar a qualidade de vida dos adolescentes, elas não substituem o tratamento no caso de problemas de saúde mental já estabelecidos.

Os autores reforçam que o acompanhamento profissional é essencial nesses casos, principalmente em um momento formador como a adolescência.

Os pesquisadores ainda afirmam que os resultados podem ajudar a orientar estudos futuros de intervenção, com o objetivo de avaliar se mudanças nesses hábitos são capazes de produzir melhorias no funcionamento acadêmico e social dos adolescentes.

articles.summary: Policiais estimaram inicialmente que o animal tinha até 1,5 metro. Agentes chamaram especialista para capturar o jacaré.
articles.body:
Um jacaré de 2,5 metros avançou contra policiais que tentavam retirá-lo do quintal de uma casa na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos . Os agentes inicialmente estimaram que o animal tivesse entre 1,2 e 1,5 metro, mas descobriram que ele era muito maior. Veja no vídeo acima.

O caso aconteceu no dia 10, mas as imagens da operação foram divulgadas na segunda-feira (14) pelo Gabinete do Xerife do Condado de Manatee.

No vídeo, os policiais tentam retirar o jacaré do quintal e levá-lo para um lago do outro lado da rua. Quando os agentes se aproximam, porém, o animal reage e avança contra eles, fazendo com que recuem.

Diante da dificuldade para controlar o jacaré, os policiais chamaram um especialista para ajudar na captura.

O profissional conseguiu capturar o animal e, depois, medir o jacaré. Foi então que os agentes descobriram que haviam subestimado bastante o tamanho dele. O animal tinha 2,54 metros de comprimento.

Após ser retirado do quintal, o jacaré foi levado para um local seguro.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Complete failure to protect babies' and 'Sterling mess'
articles.summary: The landmark public inquiry into Lucy Letby's murders and attempted murders is the focus of several of today's papers.
articles.body:
Most of the front pages highlight the finding of an inquiry that some of the babies killed by the former nurse Lucy Letby could have been saved if consultants and hospital management had acted after concerns were first raised.

The Daily Mirror describes the report as "damning". The Daily Express says cot cameras will now be used to protect babies in neonatal units.

The Daily Telegraph leads with government proposals to give mayors the power to oversee water companies in England and Wales, in line with Andy Burnham's plans to increase state control of utilities.

The paper says there'll be nine new regional bodies tasked with setting company objectives, and holding bosses to account over bills, shortages and sewage discharges.

The Times reports that the government is considering sending military support to Saudi Arabia to counter attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

A defence source says a small team of military advisers was sent to Riyadh this week in response to a Saudi request.

The Guardian says the Telegraph and Reform UK are facing accusations of undermining journalism and eroding trust, after Nigel Farage's party gave the newspaper stories that were about to be broken by other outlets.

The Telegraph published the details of two £36m donations to Reform shortly after The Sunday Times approached the party for a comment about the story. Neither Reform nor the Telegraph has commented.

"Russian spies recruiting UK teenagers" is the front page headline in the i Paper. The paper say analysis by the think-tank The Institute for Strategic Dialogue has found that Moscow is recruiting young British people willing to carry out acts of violence.

They are approached in online groups and offered money, guns and training on making explosives and poisons. The i Paper says at least two attacks have already taken place in connection with one of the groups.

The Daily Mail says several copies of a new book by Princess Diana's brother Earl Spencer, have been stolen from a lorry in the Netherlands.

The paper describes the book as explosive and says theories about who broke into the lorry range from a gang of opportunistic thieves to a misguided but highly informed supporter of the Royal Family.

After finding there was a "complete failure to protect babies" under Letby's care, the inquiry chair, Lady Justice Thirlwall, has called for cot cameras or monitors to be used on neonatal units in hospitals, the Daily Express reports. Letby is serving 15 whole-life prison terms for murdering seven babies and attempting to murder seven more.

articles.body: PewDiePie has found himself at the centre of an unexpected online debate after an old family vlog resurfaced, showing his three-year-old son Björn wearing dresses. What began as a playful moment during a family outing quickly became a talking point across social media, with viewers split over the clip. While some defended Felix and Marzia’s approach to parenting, others criticised the decision and drew comparisons to unrelated online controversies.PewDiePie son dress controversy sparks mixed reactionsThe footage comes from PewDiePie’s July 30 vlog, “Earthquake by Mount Fuji,” which follows Felix, his wife Marzia and their young son during family life in Japan.At one point, Björn appears wearing one of his mother’s dresses while walking around the home. The moment is presented casually, with Felix reacting positively as his son moves through the room.Later, the family visits a supermarket, where Björn tries on a yellow dress made for children his age. There is no indication in the footage that the moment was intended as a major statement. Instead, it appears within the ordinary, playful rhythm of a family vlog.Felix also connected the moment to his own childhood, recalling how his mother responded when he wore a dress at the age of two.“I did the same when I was two years old. My mom told me, 'Who doesn't want to wear a dress, right?'”That comment became one of the most discussed parts of the clip as viewers debated whether the scene should be treated simply as a child experimenting with clothing.On YouTube, several viewers responded warmly. Some shared their own childhood memories, while others praised Felix and Marzia for allowing their son to enjoy himself without making the clothing choice into a larger issue.One commenter wrote:“'i did the same when i was 2 yo...my mom told me, 'who doesn't wanna wear a dress?' that healed something in me,”Another viewer defended the family against criticism:“Commenting to say I'm sorry your comments are now getting flooded with hate. You guys are doing wonderfully raising Bjorn as first-time parents. Don't let them get to you,”The response on X was noticeably more divided.Some users questioned the parenting decision and brought up other internet personalities as comparisons. One post asked:“Why is PewDiePie buying dresses for his son? Is he trying to go the Kris Tyson route?”Another critic wrote:“I'm convinced everyone in front of a camera or who desires to be in front of a camera - are not normal people. None of these people are normal,”Those posts reflect individual reactions online rather than established facts about Björn or his family.PewDiePie plans to end regular family vlogsThe renewed attention also comes as PewDiePie prepares to step away from regular vlogging involving his young son.In a May 23 video titled “Ending the vlogs,” Felix explained that Björn’s growing presence in family life made it increasingly difficult to continue documenting their lives without making the child a central part of the channel.“Björn is turning 3 in July, and we've decided that we'll be ending the vlogs in September. I wanted to share this now so it doesn't come as a surprise. The main reason is that we want Björn to grow up outside of the internet and enjoy life on his own terms. If one day he wants to be part of my videos, I would never stop him, but I think that choice should be his.”The statement makes clear that the decision is centred on giving Björn greater control over his online presence as he grows older.For now, the dress clip remains a relatively small moment from a family vlog that has taken on a much larger life online. articles.body: MUMBAI: With CBI filing an FIR in the 2020 Disha Salian death case, its investigators are expected to first scrutinise documents and allegations, record statements including of police personnel who handled the initial inquiry, examine the scene and key witnesses, and carry out technical analysis before identifying suspects for questioning.Disha, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput’s manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai. A week later, Sushant was found dead at his Bandra flat. Citing “suspicious circumstances,” her father petitioned the high court seeking a murder probe. Satish Salian recorded his statement before CBI last week, and it was converted into the FIR on Sept 13.A CBI official said the FIR was registered pursuant to the court’s direction and no accused have been named at this stage, adding that names would be included if involvement is established during the probe.The FIR alleges that some public servants and police officers need to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders. It also calls for the questioning of the autopsy and forensic officials besides several others, including the building’s security guards.The FIR claims: “The persons whose roles require investigation in connection with the commission of the principal offences, criminal conspiracy, subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story, and suppression, destruction and/or fabrication of evidence include Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, Dino Morea, Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya Thackeray’s bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, Sachin Vaze, Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur, Uddhav Thackeray, Anil Deshmukh, API Ashok Devadhe, PI Jagdev Kalapad, PI Shailendra Nagarkar, PI Chimaji Adhav, PI Arjun Rajane, concerned officers of Malvani Police Station”.Satish Salian’s advocate Nilesh Ojha had alleged that Disha had information about Aaditya Thackeray’s illegal activities, shared it with Sushant Singh Rajput, who discussed it with Rhea Chakraborty, and that it was then passed to Aaditya Thackeray, after which the alleged offence and cover-up took place.With Salian alleging lapses, the high court pulled up Mumbai police for not filing an FIR in the last six years and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the probe. It observed that the police probe “raised more questions than answers.”The high court had also taken note of the fact that the post-mortem report or the accidental death report had not been given to Disha’s family. articles.body: Apple TV has been a roaring success at Emmys this year. The iPhone-makers' Apple TV proved to be the most successful studio at the Emmys 2026. The tech giant took home as many as 28 trophies in total, including six “Pluribus” wins, three for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles,” three for “Palm Royale,” one for “Slow Horses” and one for “Mr. Scorsese.” This is the first time at the top of the tally for Apple. HBO Max came in second place this year with 21 Emmys.Interestingly, Apple TV has long been compared to HBO. In fact, Apple has even been called "the new HBO" at times by some analysts. HBO boss Casey Bloys was asked by Deadline after the awards show for his reaction to Apple’s performance. In an interview conducted during HBO Max’s afterparty at the San Vicente Bungalows, Casey Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, spoke about the company’s Emmy win. Bloys was asked what he thinks about Apple TV’s performance and their first time finishing as the No. 1 platform at the Emmys?' To this, HBO CEO replied, "Well, I’m very happy because I think that they’re very handsome competitors, Zack and Jamie. Look, we’ve had very formidable competitors in going back to Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon, so [when] Apple, everybody, keeps us on our toes, I think we do our best work. It’s a little scary that they’re a trillion-dollar company, but we’ll continue to do what we do, which is put out the best shows that we can."Reacting to the wins, former Apple CEO Tim Cook wrote on Twitter, "Stories have the power to move us, inspire us, and bring us closer together. articles.title: 3 dead after news helicopter reporting for NBC L.A. crashes while covering fatal bus collision
articles.summary: An NBC Los Angeles helicopter was covering a Los Angeles Metro bus and a passenger vehicle collision, which killed two people and injured others, fire offici...
articles.body:
A helicopter affiliated with NBC Los Angeles crashed while it was covering a fatal bus collision Tuesday evening, killing the photojournalist and pilot on board and one person on the ground, the station and officials said.

The aircraft crashed in a parking lot at or near a self-storage facility in the community of Chatsworth, which is in Los Angeles' San Fernando Valley, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department and news video on the ground from NBC Los Angeles.

The helicopter was operated by Angel City Air and affiliated with the station, which said earlier on the air that it had lost contact with those on board.

"We knew it was a news chopper, we knew we'd lost contact with our people out there, and we've just received the confirmation that, in fact, NewsChopper 4 went down just before 7 o'clock tonight in Chatsworth," anchor Colleen Williams said.

"We're going to take a couple of minutes to think about that, to process and to regroup," Williams added, her voice at times emotional.

Angel City Air, which describes itself as "a full-service aerial production company," did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday night.

Three people were dead at the scene, and two others were taken to the hospital, Fire Battalion Chief Rico A. Gross said at a late-night news conference. Their conditions were unavailable.

One of the deceased appeared to be a pedestrian on the ground when the crash happened, Fire Capt. Branden Silverman said earlier.

The victims aboard the helicopter were identified by NBC Los Angeles as Angel City Air employees Eliana Moreno, an aerial photojournalist familiar to viewers of the station and its Spanish-language sister station, Telemundo 52, and pilot George Marciniw.

Moreno was born in Orange County, south of L.A., and graduated from its Chapman University with a degree in broadcast journalism and political science in 2010, NBC Los Angeles reported. She joined Angel City Air's helicopter team the same year and has reported for multiple Southern California news outlets.

Marciniw also grew up in Southern California, where he graduated from Burbank High School, according to the station.

NBC Los Angeles and Telemundo 52 issued a joint statement expressing condolences.

"We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening," the stations said. "We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives."

The helicopter crash occurred after two people were killed and others were injured in a crash between a Los Angeles Metro bus and a passenger vehicle on Nordhoff Street, according to the fire department.

It said that the bus crash happened at 5:03 p.m. and that firefighters worked to free the trapped people and assess the bus passengers.

The helicopter was one of multiple aircraft covering the crash, NBC Los Angeles reported earlier.

Fire and police personnel were nearby, Silverman said. They rushed to the crash, reported shortly before 7 p.m., and found the helicopter engulfed in flames, which had spread to nearby parked vehicles, he added.

Witness Zareh Sevanesian was driving nearby with wife Allyona when he saw the chopper's unusual descent.

"As we were driving I looked over to my left," he said. "I saw the helicopter — something didn't look right. And I told my wife, 'That helicopter is not flying right.'"

Sevanesian said he saw the helicopter gradually losing altitude. Then, he said, he pulled over near the crash as fire roared.

"It was one of the most violent fires I had ever seen," Sevanesian recalled.

He said he soon found a person down near the wreckage and three others "screaming uncontrollably."

"It was very terrifying and sad for everyone," Allyona said.

The fire department said the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration will be involved in the investigation.

Speaking near the scene Tuesday night, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said it was "a heartbreaking night for our city." She praised first responders for their quick reaction and expressed grief over those who were killed in the bus collision and the aircraft crash.

"We lost five Angelenos today," she said, "and my heart certainly goes out to the family and friends of all of those that we lost."

California Gov. Gavin Newsom also thanked first responders and offered condolences in a statement on X.

"Our hearts are with the victims and families of tonight's devastating Metro bus and helicopter crashes in Chatsworth, and with the entire NBC4 family," he said.

articles.title: South Korea court imposes $32.5m penalty on North Korea; will Pyongyang ever pay?
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A South Korean court on Wednesday directed North Korea to pay $32.5 million to Seoul for blowing up a joint liaison office in 2020 after relations bet.
articles.body: A South Korean court on Wednesday directed North Korea to pay $32.5 million to Seoul for blowing up a joint liaison office in 2020 after relations between the two countries further deteriorated following the collapse of nuclear negotiations between Pyongyang and Washington.South Korea filed the suit in 2023, describing the North's detonation of the building in the North Korean border town of Kaesong as an unlawful and violent act that breached previous agreements between the countries and severely damaged “mutual respect and trust.”While there have been cases of individuals suing the North Korean government over human rights abuses and other issues, the liaison office case was the first time the South Korean government sued Pyongyang.The ruling by the Seoul central district court was, however, symbolic as South Korea has no clear way to force Pyongyang to pay amid a diplomatic breakdown.North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in recent years has suspended all meaningful diplomacy with the South and declared it his most hostile enemy while advancing his nuclear weapons program and pursuing closer ties with Moscow and Beijing as part of what he has described as a “new Cold War.”South Korea's unification ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, said it respects the court's ruling and called for a resumption of inter-Korean diplomacy so that “all issues between the South and North can be resolved through dialogue and cooperation.”However, North Korean state media didn't immediately comment on the ruling.In June 2020, North Korea demolished the South Korean-built liaison office in Kaesong with explosives after accusing Seoul of failing to prevent North Korean defectors from sending anti-Pyongyang propaganda leaflets across the border by balloon.Pyongyang had already shut the office in January that year as it sealed its borders over coronavirus concerns, leaving the building empty when it was destroyed.The demolition was seen as a calculated show of anger aimed at pressuring Seoul amid stalled nuclear negotiations between North Korea and the United States.Former liberal South Korean President Moon Jae-in held three meetings with Kim Jong Un in 2018 and helped pave the way for Kim's first summit with then-US President Donald Trump in June that year.The diplomacy, however, collapsed after the second Kim-Trump summit in 2019, when the US rejected Pyongyang's demand for major sanctions relief in exchange for a partial dismantling of its nuclear capabilities.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Rest of World News: Five people were killed after a fire broke out in a four-storey house in a densely populated area of Hanoi, Vietnam, early on Wednesday, September 16,.
articles.body: Five people were killed after a fire broke out in a four-storey house in a densely populated area of Hanoi, Vietnam, early on Wednesday, September 16, police said. Four others escaped the building before firefighters brought the blaze under control.The fire broke out at a house in a narrow alley off Van Cao Street in Hanoi's Tay Ho Ward at around 1.50am, according to local reports. Residents raised the alarm and tried to put out the flames with available equipment, but were unable to control the fire.Hanoi police received the emergency call at about 2am and sent a command vehicle, five fire engines and nearly 40 officers and firefighters to the scene, according to local reports. Fire and rescue teams from nearby units also joined the operation.When firefighters arrived, four people had escaped, while several others were trapped inside the house, according to local reports.Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus entered the building to search for those inside. They also used water to stop the flames from spreading to the upper floors and nearby houses.The blaze was brought under control at about 2.30am and was completely extinguished 15 minutes later, Hanoi police said.Rescue teams found five people dead during a search of the building. Their bodies were handed over to medical authorities.The four-storey house had a floor area of about 60 square metres per floor. Police are investigating the cause of the fire and working to establish the identities of the victims.According to local reports, Hanoi People's Committee chairman Vũ Đại Thắng visited the site and directed authorities to support the victims' families and deal with the aftermath of the fire.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: PALAKKAD: Keralam travel vlogger Arunima I P, who is touring Afghanistan solo, said Tuesday that she was “safe”. Her post seeking help to contact the Indian embassy had triggered concern.She had shared a translated message saying she had been “arrested by mujahideen” for not having an official letter. “I’m in trouble in Afghanistan. I’m in Bamyan,” she had written. In a subsequent post, Arunima clarified that she was not taken to a police station or prison. Residents in Bamyan had asked her to show her passport, visa and travel permit.As the situation grew tense, Arunima contacted a local man who had earlier helped her reach Bamyan. articles.title: Saudi Arabia released 313 desert gazelles; 20 years later, both species had established in a vast protected desert
articles.summary: Middle East News: Across one of Saudi Arabia’s largest protected desert landscapes, a conservation experiment that began in the 1990s is still visible two decades later.
articles.body: Across one of Saudi Arabia’s largest protected desert landscapes, a conservation experiment that began in the 1990s is still visible two decades later. A total of 313 captive-bred Arabian and sand gazelles were released into Uruq Bani Ma'arid, where their movements were first followed with radio tracking. When researchers returned in 2015–2016, a large camera-trap survey showed that both species had established populations, although they used different parts of the reserve. Sand gazelles also shifted their range with the seasons, while Arabian gazelles changed their activity as temperatures rose, spending more time active at night and around dawn and dusk.Saudi Arabia gazelle reintroduction began with 313 captive-bred animalsThe gazelles belonged to two species with a long association with the Arabian Peninsula. The Arabian gazelle, Gazella arabica, and Arabian sand gazelle, Gazella marica, are both globally threatened. During the mid-to-late 1990s, groups of captive-bred sand gazelles and Arabian gazelles were released at several locations within Uruq Bani Ma'arid. The approach was spread over multiple sites and carried out over a period of roughly two to three years, rather than relying on a single release point.That detail mattered because the objective was not simply to put animals into the desert. The wider conservation strategy was to establish populations in suitable habitat where the animals could remain protected and reproduce. The early movements of the released gazelles were followed using VHF radio-tracking. It gave researchers a way of seeing where individual animals went after release and how they began occupying the protected area.Camera traps revealed where the reintroduced gazelles settled 20 years laterAccording to the study published in Journal of Arid Environments, titled ‘The conservation status of the threatened gazelles of Ar Rub’ al-Khālī, Saudi Arabia'revealed by 2015 and 2016, about 20 years had passed since the original reintroductions. Conventional wildlife surveys can be difficult across a landscape as large and remote as Uruq Bani Ma'arid, particularly when animals are dispersed across different habitats.This time, a large network of camera traps was used. The cameras provided a much broader picture than following a limited number of radio-collared animals. They could record wildlife across different parts of the protected area and over extended periods, allowing researchers to examine both distribution and relative abundance.What emerged was not a population concentrated around the original release sites. The Arabian gazelles had become established across the western part of Uruq Bani Ma'arid. Sand gazelles occupied a broader central area, with their distribution changing with the seasons.The reintroduced sand gazelles still followed seasonal habitat patternsThe sand gazelles showed a particularly clear seasonal movement. During the cooler part of the year, they moved further into the interior of the protected area. When temperatures rose, they shifted back towards the western margin. The pattern fits with the animals' established relationship with their desert habitat. Rather than remaining in one fixed section of the reserve throughout the year, they adjusted their movements as environmental conditions changed.The long-term observations also indicated that the reintroduced animals had retained habitat preferences associated with their species. Captive breeding and subsequent release had not apparently erased those behavioural patterns. For conservation programmes, that provides a useful piece of information. A population does not necessarily need to occupy every part of a protected landscape to be considered established. Its use of the landscape can instead reflect the ecological conditions it has evolved to handle.Arabian gazelles changed their activity patterns with the desert heatThe gazelles were also responding to the desert in another way: when they were active. During the hot season, Arabian gazelles shifted towards activity during the night and around dawn and dusk. Sand gazelles showed a similar, though less pronounced, seasonal change.In the cooler season, activity was more concentrated during daylight and the periods around sunrise and sunset.That change offers another glimpse into how the animals use an extreme environment. When daytime temperatures become difficult, activity can move towards cooler parts of the 24-hour cycle. Once conditions are moderate, the animals can spend more time active during daylight.Both gazelle species survived and established populations after 20 yearsThe significance of the later camera-trap survey was its timescale. Wildlife reintroductions can look promising soon after animals are released, when the focus is often on survival and the first signs of reproduction. A population that remains present decades later provides a different kind of evidence.In Uruq Bani Ma'arid, both reintroduced species had established populations roughly two decades after the original releases. Their distributions were different, but neither had simply disappeared from the protected landscape. The Arabian gazelle had become established mainly in the western portion, while the sand gazelle had spread through much of the central area and shifted its range seasonally.The findings therefore went beyond confirming that released animals had survived. They showed that the two species had continued to use the desert in ways broadly consistent with their known ecological preferences.A protected landscape made the reintroduction possibleUruq Bani Ma'arid occupies part of the western Rub’ al-Khali, one of the great desert landscapes of the Arabian Peninsula. Its enormous scale creates conditions very different from those found in a small wildlife enclosure or intensively managed reserve. The 12,684-square-kilometre protected area offered enough space for the animals to spread into different habitats and alter their movements according to the season.That scale also explains why the camera-trap work was useful. Following animals individually across such a large and difficult landscape would have obvious practical limits. A broad array of cameras could instead collect observations from many locations and build up a picture over time.Reintroduced gazelles retained distinct habitat preferencesAlthough both species were released as part of the same wider restoration effort, their later distributions were not identical. Arabian gazelles were associated more strongly with the western side of the protected area. Sand gazelles were more widely distributed through the centre, while also making a pronounced seasonal movement towards the interior during cooler conditions and back towards the western edge during hotter periods.Those differences are important because successful restoration does not necessarily mean making two species behave in the same way. Each species brought its own ecological preferences into the restored landscape. The fact that those patterns remained visible years after captive breeding and release suggests that the animals were able to resume aspects of their natural habitat use.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
